subject: Cross-connect KEK derivation and secrets guardrails
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-connect KEK derivation and secrets guardrails

Folks — attaching a short proposal for the cross-connect key-encryption-key (KEK) derivation approach we discussed in Friday's run-through. High-level asks:

- Validate threat model and any compliance gaps for per-tenant KEKs derived over the private interconnect.
- Confirm whether Acme can accept a client-side derived KEK (HKDF) wrapped by our HSM root, or if you require custodial KEKs exclusively in your HSM.
- Review the rotation windows and the proposed emergency zeroize procedure.

Notes in the attachment: kek-derivation-spec.md (text). Quick summary here:
- Each tenant has a per-tenant root_secret generated in customer-controlled KMS (BYOK).
- On cross-connect establishment we derive a session_salt tied to the physical circuit ID + timestamp and run HKDF to produce a per-connection KEK (AES-256-GCM wrapping key).
- Encrypted data keys (EDKs) are wrapped with that KEK; we also double-wrap with an HSM-wrapped root for long-term archival.
- Rotation: rolling rewrap every 30 days; emergency rotate within 1 hour using a staged fallback (read-only fallback variant while rewrap completes).

A few open items (please call these out in replies):
1) Does Acme have policy constraints about deriving keys from cross-connect metadata?
2) Any required formal evidence for HSM provenance (serial numbers, attestation docs) beyond SOC2/ISO evidence?
3) Are our proposed rewrap/rollback semantics acceptable for your DR testing (we target <10s read-only window in the worst case)?

Attachments: kek-derivation-spec.md, crossconnect-network-diff.patch

Thanks — want to get alignment before we write the design doc for the private deploy runbook.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
(attachment: kek-derivation-spec.md (text/markdown))

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@acmecloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, infra-sec@acmecloud.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-connect KEK derivation and secrets guardrails

Sean — thanks for the detailed primer, this is helpful. Quick feedback from Acme ops/security after an initial review: 

1) Metadata-derived keys: we prefer deterministic derivation only when the inputs are strictly non-secret (e.g., circuit ID) plus a tenant-owned secret; we cannot accept derivation that could be recomputed by an intermediary network device. If you include a tenant BYOK root and mix with circuit ID + ephemeral nonce we can sign off on the model.

2) Double-wrap model is fine, provided the outer HSM-wrapped blob is generated inside our HSM onshore (we require HSM attestation and key material never exported in plaintext). We will need: HSM manufacturer/model, firmware hash, and attestations for the specific HSM instance you'll use.

3) Rotation windows / rollback: 30 days is OK for primary keys, but we will require a documented emergency rewrap playbook with a maximum RTO of 2 hours for tenant writes during an incident (we know you aim for <10s; we will test to your target but require the documented 2-hour fallback as contractual coverage).

4) Logging & audit: every wrap/unwrap operation must emit an immutable audit record to Acme's audit stream (we can consume a signed webhook or pull from an SFTP drop with signed manifests). Records must include operation, key-id, HSM-csn, operator-principal, and UTC timestamp.

5) Evidence: for SOC2/ISO check we still want per-HSM attestation (quote/provisioning records), and a copy of the KMS access policy you'll enforce for Redwood-managed ops accounts. The PDF "acme-ops-questions.pdf" (attached) lists the initial evidence items.

I'll loop in infra-sec and we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the playbook and the attestation expectations.

On quoted text:
> Each tenant has a per-tenant root_secret generated in customer-controlled KMS (BYOK).

That is a hard requirement for us — the tenant root secret must remain in our control at all times.

—Alex
Alex Ruiz
Security Architect — Acme Cloud
(attachment: acme-ops-questions.pdf (application/pdf))

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Cross-connect KEK derivation and secrets guardrails

Alex — appreciate the clear list. We'll prepare the evidence bundle and a short runbook for the emergency rewrap path. Action items for Redwood here: 

- Produce HSM inventory (model, serials, firmware) and provide attestation artifacts — target: EOD Wed 2026-09-02.
- Draft the emergency rewrap playbook with explicit RTO guarantees (we'll include the staged read-only fallback, and the manual override if automated rewrap fails).
- Add signed audit record support: we'll prototype a signed webhook and an SFTP manifest export for you to consume.

I've put the drive link with a working directory: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/KEK-derivation-spec — we'll drop the artifacts there as they become available.

CC'ing Tessa for deployment sequencing.

—Monica
Monica Patel

Quick follow-up with sequencing and owners. Proposed staged rollout: 

1) Design freeze and evidence handoff (Monica) — target 2026-09-02.
2) Non-prod validation over an isolated VPC + test HSM tenant (Infra) — 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-11.
3) Joint DR run and audit ingestion test with Acme (Ops + Acme infra-sec) — 2026-09-15.
4) Production ramp: start with 5 pilot tenants on the private cross-connect, monitor audit stream and rewrap behavior for 7 days, then expand.

Open items for our infra runbook: the KEK derivation spec needs a short section on clock skew tolerance and nonce reuse protection — I added a small patch (crossconnect-network-diff.patch) to the drive. Also attaching a trimmed spec draft: kek-derivation-spec.md.

If everyone agrees I'll schedule the 30-minute sync with Acme infra-sec for Thursday 2026-09-03 10:00 PT. Confirmable by Alex?

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
